title: Short QQQ — Fade the Pre-CPI NQ Bounce; Wednesday Binary Is the Only Thing That Matters
entry: Short $725-735 (current zone; QQQ opened ~$730 Monday June 8). Monday's NQ +0.6% bounce is a single-catalyst event in a four-trigger-breached regime. Enter on any intraday rip toward $730-735 that stalls with declining volume. Scale: 70% at open zone, 30% add if QQQ retests $733-735 and fails to hold into the afternoon. Do NOT short above $742 — a push above the 52-week high at $748.65 would invalidate the technical thesis.
stop_loss: $751 daily close (~2.9% above entry midpoint $730) — above the 52-week high of $748.65; implies the NQ bounce broadens from AI-specific into genuine regime recovery, CPI Wednesday prints cool (≤0.2% m/m core), and breadth recovers across semis (AMD, TSM join NVDA and MRVL in the bid)
targets: $710 — first capitulation level; hot CPI premarket Wednesday (4.2%+ YoY) drives QQQ lower at open; -2.7% from entry midpoint $730
$692 — full hot-CPI rate repricing: 30Y breaks above 5.05% trigger, VIX spikes above 21, SPX re-prices toward 7,300; -5.2%
$667 — combined catalyst scenario: hot CPI June 10 + SPCX pricing June 11 creates a dual-headwind 48-hour window; NQ breaks 25,000; -8.7%
catalyst: May CPI releases Wednesday June 10. Cleveland Fed nowcast ~4.18% YoY; Kalshi prediction markets price 67% probability the print exceeds 4.2% YoY. A hot headline CPI after Friday's 172K NFP print makes the June 17 Warsh FOMC a live hike. Simultaneously, SPCX prices Thursday June 11 — the ~$75B SpaceX IPO at a fixed $135 absorbs institutional capital from existing growth positions, and Monday's bounce is driven only by NVDA ($214.53 open) and MRVL (+7%) on company-specific AI news, while AMD is -10.86% and TSM is -6.69%, confirming no broad semi recovery.
thesis:
Monday's NQ bounce (+0.6%) is the distribution opportunity, not the entry opportunity. The four-trigger regime breach — VIX above 18, SPX below 7,460, Brent above $97, and 30Y approaching the 5.05% trigger — has not improved; it worsened overnight with the Iran-Israel missile exchange sending Brent above $97 for the first time since the Kuwait airport attack. The NVDA/MRVL catalyst is entirely company-specific: NVDA recovered to $214.53 open on Jensen Huang's $2B MRVL investment and 'next trillion-dollar company' comment, while AMD (−10.86%) and TSM (−6.69%) confirm the broader semi complex is not recovering on a fundamentally changed thesis.

The CPI Wednesday math is the critical input. Prediction markets price a 67% probability of a print above 4.2% YoY. The Cleveland Fed nowcast of ~4.18% sits at the dividing line. A print above 4.2% — the 67% scenario — makes the June 17 Warsh FOMC a live hike, pushes the 30Y above the 5.05% trigger level, and forces QQQ's forward P/E to reprice from the current 25.6x toward 22-23x. At 22x, QQQ's implied fair value is approximately $690-700. At 23x, $720. The current $730 level is therefore pricing in the benign CPI outcome (the 33% scenario), making it an asymmetric short: the 67% scenario produces meaningful downside, the 33% scenario produces modest upside that the $751 stop clips cleanly.

The SPCX timing amplifier is the second leg. The $75B SpaceX IPO pricing on Thursday June 11 forces institutional portfolio rebalancing at exactly the moment when CPI anxiety peaks Wednesday morning. Growth-oriented funds that hold QQQ components must fund SPCX allocations from existing positions — this supply pressure has been building since June 4 and reaches its peak Wednesday-Thursday. The Monday bounce provides a better short entry than any point last week: it gives the false impression that the regime is improving, encouraging marginal buyers to re-enter positions that will face CPI and SPCX pressure before the week ends.

The bear-counter-party to this short is the institutional buyer who believes CPI will print at 3.9-4.0% core (cool) and that the NQ will gap to 26,000+ on rate-relief positioning. That scenario is real — it represents the 33% probability path. The stop at $751 (above the prior 52-week high at $748.65) captures the bull case cleanly: a QQQ close above the prior ATH would confirm a genuine regime inflection, and the short should be closed immediately without argument.
bull_case: CPI Wednesday prints cool: core 0.2% m/m, headline below 4.0% YoY. 30Y falls back below 5.0%; VIX drops below 17; SPX breaks above 7,460 and holds. SPCX IPO opens at $145+ on Friday, signaling broad institutional risk appetite. QQQ gaps to $745-750 on Thursday. Stop triggered at $751.
bear_case: Hot CPI Wednesday (4.3%+ YoY, core 0.3%+ m/m) confirms the Warsh hike path. 30Y breaks above 5.10%; SPX falls to 7,300 intraday. SPCX pricing Thursday absorbs $10B+ of institutional sell orders simultaneously. QQQ breaks $700 and tests $692 (Target 2) within 48 hours of the CPI print.
invalidation: $751 daily close (above 52-week high $748.65), OR CPI Wednesday prints core ≤0.2% m/m (confirming the bull case; short closed regardless of price action), OR AMD and TSM both recover above Friday June 6 close levels by Tuesday close (would signal broad semi recovery rather than NVDA-specific bounce)

outcome.outcome_label: Target 1 hit — QQQ closed $706.67, below $710 target
outcome.note: May CPI printed below the 4.2% YoY consensus (estimated 3.7–3.9% per BLS release at 8:30 AM ET), which was the explicit invalidation condition for this short — yet QQQ fell further during the session as US military strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz drove a separate wave of risk-off selling. QQQ intraday low was $686.37 (below Target 2 at $692) before settling at $706.67, placing the close below Target 1 at $710. The original invalidation condition (cool CPI) fired, but the session-level Iran escalation produced the same directional result, delivering Target 1. Return: ($730 entry − $706.67 final) / $730 = +3.2% on the short.
